message.content:
● Review: PR #812 — In-place merge of duplicate members

   Solid PR overall: good test coverage (484 lines of backend tests, frontend dialog tests), reuse of the existing tree-merge machinery instead of forking, a rich activity payload anticipating undo (#572),
   correct route ordering, i18n parity (only en/de exist), and a CHANGELOG entry. But I found several real issues, two of which I'd call blockers.

   Blockers / Majors

   1. Vital-event mirror breaks after a merge — backend/app/services/member_merge.py:469
   _repoint_member_links(db, EventMemberLink, ...) transfers all of remove's event links — including the derived birth/death mirror events, which are plain Event rows of type birth/death linked via
   EventMemberLink. Two consequences, both verified against _sync_vital_event (members.py:732):
   • If both members have a mirror birth (or death) event — the common case for duplicates — keep ends up linked to two birth events. _sync_vital_event assumes one (events[0], ordered by random UUID), so
     future edits update one arbitrarily and the stale duplicate stays visible in keep's timeline.
   • If the merge changes keep's date_of_birth/date_of_death/birthplace/cemetery via field choice "b", the mirror is never re-synced — update_member does this (members.py:876-895), the merge route doesn't.
     The merge must dedupe same-type vital events (honoring the user's field choice) and/or call _sync_vital_event afterward.

   2. Bridge-person drift — members.py merge route
   BRIDGE_SYNC_FIELDS overlaps CONFLICT_FIELDS almost entirely (names, dates, birthplace, cemetery, additional_data…). If keep is a bridge person and field choices adopt remove's values, the counterpart in
   the other tree is not synced — update_member calls _sync_bridge_person (members.py:897), the merge path skips it. There's a drift-detection feature that may paper over this later, but the merge knowingly
   creates the drift it then relies on detecting.

   3. Cycle guard is over-broad and misleads — member_merge.py:418
   find_parent_cycle_members(remaining_members, simulated_relations) rejects the merge if any parent cycle exists anywhere in the simulated graph — including pre-existing cycles unrelated to the merged pair
   (relation creation has no cycle guard, and the quality report itself treats cycles as a pre-existing, informational finding). Result: one bad cycle elsewhere in the tree disables all member merges, with
   the misleading message "This merge would create a relationship cycle". The guard should only reject cycles involving keep.id. Related UX gap: the preview endpoint doesn't run the check, so users resolve
   all field conflicts and only get the 400 on confirm.

   4. Stale frontend stores after merge — useQualityReportStore.ts:83-95
   mergeMembers refreshes only the report and member list. It skips invalidateDerivedViews() (which the normal member-delete path calls, useMemberStore.ts:134) and doesn't clear the per-tree domain stores
   (useEventStore, useStoryStore, useGalleryStore, useTaskStore) — yet the merge re-points exactly that content. Already-initialized stores serve stale data (wrong statistics, transferred events invisible)
   until reconnect. This is the first in-place member deletion in the app, so the gap is new.

   Minors

   • Data loss by default: buildInitialResolutionState defaults every conflict to "a" (mergeUtils.ts:60). For one-sided conflicts (keep empty, remove has data — which compute_conflicts does report), clicking
     through with defaults silently discards remove's values. reconcile_bridge_fields defaults one-sided fields to the non-empty side (merge.py:349); this dialog should too. Same for image_data when only
     remove has a photo — not even reported as a conflict, so it's lost invisibly.
   • Double success toast: the dialog toasts "Members merged." and then onMerged() triggers the identical toast again in QualityReportView.tsx:218.
   • Silent preview failure: MergeMembersDialog.tsx catches preview errors with setPreview(null) — no error UI, permanently disabled Merge button, no explanation.
   • Preview transfer counts overstate: compute_member_merge_preview counts all of remove's relations/links, but duplicates and self-relations are dropped during the actual merge — the promised "N will be
     transferred" can be wrong.
   • Convention deviation: the dialog calls TreeService directly for the preview (AGENTS.md says components only call store actions). MergeTreesDialog sets the same precedent, but it's still a documented
     violation — a store pass-through would be cleaner.
   • Style: member_merge.py imports private names (_norm, _to_snake_case) from app.services.merge — promote them to public or inline them. SimpleNamespace fakes passed as list[Relation] to
     find_parent_cycle_members is a type-hint lie. Service layer raising HTTPException is consistent with the codebase, so acceptable.

   Nits

   • mergeMembers silently succeeds with no active tree → false success toast for a destructive op.
   • No undo grace period, unlike normal member deletion (defensible given the confirm dialog, but a conscious inconsistency).
   • Dead defensive code: the two Selects filter out each other's value, so the same-member guard is unreachable.
   • GET merge-preview requires get_writable_tree — defensible as a pre-write step, but semantically odd for a GET.

   Challenges to the design

   • The vital-event transfer reveals a modeling ambiguity: mirror events are indistinguishable from user-authored events, so "union all event links" can't be right in general. The merge needs
     vital-event-aware dedup, not generic link union.
   • Why simulate-and-DFS the whole graph? The guard loads every member and relation in the tree to check a property that only depends on ancestry reachable from keep. A DFS from keep over the simulated
     edges is cheaper and, more importantly, makes the "cycles involving keep only" fix natural.
   • Activity action is "update" on keep — there's no "delete" entry for remove and no distinct "merge" action. The undo payload is forward-looking (#572), but activity consumers filtering on delete will
     miss that a person vanished. Worth a dedicated action type now rather than a migration later.
   • No concurrency handling: two editors merging overlapping pairs concurrently can interleave deletes/re-points within no transaction isolation beyond the single commit. Probably acceptable at self-hosted
     scale, but it's unacknowledged. whats your take on this

@router.patch("/members/collapsed", status_code=204)
def update_member_collapsed(
    payload: list[MemberCollapsedUpdate],
    tree: Tree = Depends(get_writable_tree),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
):
    """Persist collapse/expand state for many members in one round-trip.

    Declared before ``/members/{member_id}`` so the literal ``collapsed`` path
    isn't captured as a member id. Unknown ids are silently skipped.
    """
    if not payload:
        return
    ids = [p.id for p in payload]
    members = {
        m.id: m
        for m in db.scalars(
            select(Member).where(Member.tree_id == tree.id, Member.id.in_(ids))
        )
    }
    for p in payload:
        member = members.get(p.id)
        if member is not None:
            member.is_collapsed = p.is_collapsed
    db.commit()

content.text:
My take: real gap, but I'd rank it with the nits, not the blockers — don't let it hold up the PR.

**Why it's low-stakes here:** this is a self-hosted app; the realistic actor count per tree is small (owner + a few editors), and merging duplicate members is an infrequent, deliberate curation action, not a high-frequency write path. The odds of two people merging overlapping pairs in the same few hundred milliseconds are low.

**But the failure mode is worse than "probably fine," so it's worth naming precisely:** there's no row lock (no `with_for_update()`), so under Postgres's default READ COMMITTED, two overlapping merges (e.g. A merges X→Y while B merges Y→Z) can both read Y before either commits. Whichever transaction commits second either:
- hits a `StaleDataException`/IntegrityError when it tries to UPDATE or DELETE a `Member` row the other transaction already removed — surfaces as an ugly 500, not a clean error, or
- in the FK re-point tables (`EventMemberLink` etc.), re-points rows that then get orphaned by the other transaction's delete of the same member, if ordering lands wrong.

Neither of these silently corrupts data in a way a user wouldn't notice — SQLAlchemy's unit-of-work raises on unexpected row counts — but it does mean the second editor gets a stack-trace-flavored 500 instead of a sane "this member was already merged, refresh and try again."

**What I'd actually suggest, and at what priority:** file it as a fast-follow, not a blocker. The fix is cheap — wrap `merge_members_in_place` in `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` on `keep`/`remove`, or just catch the stale-object case in the route and return 409 with a message telling the client to refresh. I would not build anything heavier (locking service, optimistic version columns) for this app's scale.

If you want, I can turn this whole review into the actual PR comment/summary, or start on the two blockers (vital-event dedup + bridge sync) first since those are the ones that produce silently wrong data rather than just a bad error page.

Here's how I'd triage it for an actual review post — not everything above deserves a comment.

**Must fix before merge (request changes):**
1. Vital-event mirror dedup — silently wrong data in the UI, the core "merge should just work" promise broken.
2. Bridge-person drift — merge creates the exact inconsistency the drift-detector exists to catch; shipping a feature that knowingly generates bugs for another feature to clean up later is backwards.
3. Cycle guard scoped to `keep.id` only — as written, one unrelated pre-existing cycle anywhere in the tree disables merging entirely, with a misleading error. This will hit real users, not an edge case.
4. Frontend store staleness (`invalidateDerivedViews` + domain stores) — same category as #1/#2: user acts, data looks unchanged until reload.
5. One-sided conflict defaults discarding data (`buildInitialResolutionState` defaulting to "a", plus `image_data` not even surfaced as a conflict) — I'd bump this out of "minor" into the same tier as the blockers. Silent data loss on a destructive, irreversible operation is worse than a display bug.

**Worth flagging, non-blocking (reviewer comments, author's call on this PR vs. follow-up):**
- Double success toast — trivial, fix now.
- Silent preview failure with no error UI — cheap fix, do it now.
- Preview transfer counts overstating what actually transfers — misleads users right before a destructive confirm; low effort to correct.
- Private-import/style nits (`_norm`, `_to_snake_case`, `SimpleNamespace` type lie) — mention, don't block on it.

**Mention once, then drop:**
- TreeService-from-component convention deviation — already precedented by `MergeTreesDialog`, so it's consistent-with-existing-sin rather than new debt. Note it, don't ask for a rewrite.
- No active tree → false success toast, dead same-member guard code, GET-requires-writable-tree — genuine nits, low value, bundle into one "minor cleanup" comment thread instead of separate threads.

**Don't put in the review at all — raise as follow-up issues/discussion instead:**
- No undo grace period — defensible given the confirm dialog; not this PR's job to fix.
- Activity action modeling ("update" vs. a real "merge"/"delete" entry) — legitimate architectural point but tied to the not-yet-built undo work (#572); premature to demand now.
- Concurrency handling — as discussed, real but low-priority for this app's scale; a fast-follow ticket, not a merge blocker.
- The "why simulate-and-DFS the whole graph" efficiency point — folds naturally into the cycle-guard fix (#3) once that's scoped to `keep.id`, so it resolves itself rather than needing separate callout.

Want me to draft this as the actual `gh pr review` comment body, or file the follow-up items (concurrency, activity action type) as separate GitHub issues?

I now have a complete picture. Here is the plan.

---

# Implementation Plan — PR #812 review fixes

## Key architectural constraint discovered (affects items 1 & 2)

`backend/app/services/member_merge.py` is imported by `backend/app/api/routes/members.py` (line 68). The helpers the review says to reuse — `_sync_vital_event` (members.py:732), `_sync_bridge_person` (members.py:178), `_event_updates_allowed` (members.py:629) — live in the **route module**. The service therefore cannot call them without a circular import. Two options recur below:

- **Option A (recommended, least churn):** do the post-merge fix-ups in the route handler `merge_members` (members.py:389-472), after `merge_members_in_place` returns and before `db.commit()`. The route already orchestrates activity logging + SSE, and has `user`/`tree` in scope.
- **Option B:** extract `_sync_vital_event` + `_event_updates_allowed` (and optionally `_sync_bridge_person`) into a shared service module and import from both. Cleaner separation but a bigger diff and more test surface.

The plan below assumes Option A unless noted. Whichever is chosen, items 1 and 2 both add post-merge sync that can touch a second tree (the bridge counterpart's), which must then get its own `content_changed`/activity — see the interaction notes.

---

## Item 1 — Vital-event mirror breaks after merge (MUST FIX)

**Problem confirmed.** `merge_members_in_place` (member_merge.py:263) calls `_repoint_member_links(EventMemberLink,...)`, transferring *all* of `remove`'s event links onto `keep`, including derived birth/death mirror `Event` rows. Two failure modes:
- (a) keep + remove each have a birth mirror event → keep ends up linked to two birth events. `_sync_vital_event` (members.py:753) does `events[0]` and assumes exactly one; the second lingers as a stale duplicate in keep's timeline.
- (b) field choice "b" changes keep's `date_of_birth`/`date_of_death`/`birthplace`/`cemetery` → the mirror event is never re-synced (the merge path never calls `_sync_vital_event`, unlike `update_member` at members.py:882-893).

**Fix (route, post-merge — members.py `merge_members`):** after `merge_members_in_place` returns, before `record_activity`:
1. Gate on `_event_updates_allowed(db, tree, user)` to match `update_member` and avoid partial failures when Events is disabled/restricted.
2. **Dedup** keep's vital mirror events: for each of `"birth"`/`"death"`, query `Event` rows of that type linked to `keep.id` via `EventMemberLink` (same query shape as `_sync_vital_event`, members.py:741-752), ordered deterministically; if more than one, keep the first and `db.delete` the rest (their `EventMemberLink` rows cascade — confirm cascade or delete the links explicitly).
3. **Resync** the surviving event to keep's post-merge resolved fields: call `_sync_vital_event(db, tree, keep, "birth", keep.date_of_birth, keep.birthplace)` and `..."death", keep.date_of_death, keep.cemetery)`. This aligns the date and backfills location using the existing #659/#769-safe logic.
4. Publish an extra `tree.content_changed` with `domain: "event"` for `tree` (mirroring `update_member` at members.py:929-935) so timelines refresh — but note item 4 will already broaden domain refresh; keep this consistent.

**Interaction with item 2:** if keep is a bridge person, the resynced/deduped vital event lives only in keep's tree; the counterpart's vital fields are handled by item 2's `_sync_bridge_person`, but the counterpart's *own* mirror events are not touched here (update_member has the same limitation — acceptable, note it).

**Decision to flag:** doing dedup only when `_event_updates_allowed` means a restricted-events editor's merge could still leave a duplicate birth event. The duplicate is a real integrity problem independent of the flag. Recommend: run **dedup unconditionally** (integrity cleanup, like the FK cleanup already done in the merge) but gate only the **date/location resync** on `_event_updates_allowed`. Call this out for the reviewer.

**Tests (`backend/tests/test_member_merge.py`):**
- keep + remove each have a birth mirror event → after merge, keep has exactly one birth event with keep's resolved date (extends the pattern of `test_event_link_transferred` / `test_event_link_duplicate_dropped`).
- field choice "b" adopts remove's `date_of_birth`/`birthplace` → keep's single birth mirror event reflects remove's date/location afterwards (builds on `test_field_choice_b_adopts_remove_value` at line 319).
- events-restricted editor path (if you gate resync) → no crash, links still repointed.

---

## Item 2 — Bridge-person drift (MUST FIX)

**Problem confirmed.** `BRIDGE_SYNC_FIELDS` (bridge.py:16-34) overlaps `CONFLICT_FIELDS` (merge.py:109-121) almost entirely. If keep is a bridge person and field choices adopt remove's values, keep's counterpart in the other tree is never synced. `update_member` handles this via `_sync_bridge_person` (members.py:897); the merge path does not.

**Fix (route, post-merge — members.py `merge_members`):**
1. Compute the set of person-fields that actually changed on keep due to the merge. `merge_members_in_place` already captures `keep_before` (member_merge.py:225) and returns it inside `details["merge"]["keep_before"]`. Either read it from `details`, or (cleaner) have `merge_members_in_place` also return an explicit `changed_fields` dict. Recommend adding `changed_fields` to the return tuple to avoid reaching into the activity payload. Build `changed = {f: getattr(keep, f) for f in CONFLICT_FIELDS if getattr(keep, f) != keep_before[f]}`.
2. Call `_sync_bridge_person(db, keep, changed, user)` (members.py:178). It already filters to `BRIDGE_SYNC_FIELDS`, checks the `tree_links` feature + write access, copies media cross-tree, and returns `(status, synced_tree)`.
3. If `synced_tree` is returned, publish `tree.content_changed` (domain member) + `invalidate_stats` for it, exactly like `update_member` (members.py:937-944).

**Interaction — bridge inherited case:** `merge_members_in_place` may have just *inherited* remove's bridge onto keep (member_merge.py:280-285), setting `keep.linked_member_id` to remove's counterpart. Running `_sync_bridge_person(keep, changed, user)` then pushes keep's resolved identity onto that newly-inherited counterpart — desirable. But the route already logs a bridge activity entry for that counterpart tree (members.py:427-449). Ensure the new `_sync_bridge_person` call and the existing counterpart activity/SSE don't double-publish or conflict for the same tree. Flag this: the "changed_fields" sync and the "inherited link" activity may target the **same** counterpart tree — consolidate the SSE/`invalidate_stats` calls so each tree is published once.

**Signature change flagged:** returning `changed_fields` (or the resolved-changes) from `merge_members_in_place` is the cleanest wiring and keeps the route from parsing `details`.

**Tests (`backend/tests/test_member_merge.py`):** extend the existing bridge tests (`test_bridge_link_inherited_onto_keep_and_logged_in_other_tree` line 383, `test_bridge_link_dissolved...` line 432):
- keep is a bridge person; merge adopts remove's `date_of_birth`/`last_name` via field choice "b" → counterpart in the other tree now has the new values (feature enabled, writer access).
- feature off / no access → counterpart unchanged, no crash (mirrors `_sync_bridge_person`'s `skipped_no_access`).

---

## Item 3 — Cycle guard is over-broad (MUST FIX)

**Problem confirmed.** member_merge.py:193-216 simulates the whole tree's relations and calls `find_parent_cycle_members(remaining_members, simulated_relations)` (quality_checks.py:45), which returns cycle members *anywhere* in the graph. Any pre-existing unrelated cycle → every merge in that tree 400s with "This merge would create a relationship cycle". Relation-creation elsewhere has no cycle guard, and the quality report treats cycles as informational, so this is inconsistent and misleading.

**Fix:** scope the check to cycles **reachable from/involving `keep.id` after the merge**. Replace the whole-graph simulation with a targeted DFS:
1. Build a post-merge parent adjacency in memory: iterate `all_relations`, remap `remove.id → keep.id` on both endpoints, drop self-edges, keep only `relation_type == "parent"` edges (child `from_member_id` → parent `to_member_id`), dedup.
2. Run a DFS starting **from `keep.id`** walking the parent chain; if the traversal revisits `keep.id` (a node on the current stack loops back), it's a merge-created/merge-involving cycle → 400. A cycle not reachable from keep is left alone.
3. This removes the need to fetch `remaining_members` and to build `SimpleNamespace` fakes (ties into item 8).

**Preview decision (flagged):** `get_member_merge_preview` (members.py:606) currently does **not** run any cycle check, so users resolve all conflicts then hit a 400 on confirm. Recommend surfacing the scoped check earlier: add a boolean like `would_create_cycle` to `MemberMergePreviewOut` (schema `backend/app/schemas/merge.py`) computed by `compute_member_merge_preview`, and have the frontend dialog disable Merge + show a message when true. This is a schema field addition (no DB migration — response-only). If you prefer to keep scope tight, at minimum keep the confirm-time 400 but this is the better UX. **This interacts with item 6** (error UI) — the cycle-preview message and the preview-failure message are different states.

**Extract a helper:** put the scoped "does merging remove into keep create a parent cycle reachable from keep" logic in a small function (in member_merge.py or quality_checks.py) so both the confirm path and preview path call the same code.

**Tests:**
- `test_member_merge.py`: keep `test_merge_creates_cycle_is_rejected` (line 96) passing under the new logic. **Add** a test: a pre-existing cycle among *unrelated* members does **not** block merging two other members (this is the regression the fix targets).
- If adding `would_create_cycle` to preview: a preview test asserting the flag flips true for a merge that would loop keep's parent chain.
- `backend/tests/test_quality.py`: unaffected (`find_parent_cycle_members` signature unchanged if you add a separate scoped helper rather than modifying it).

---

## Item 4 — Stale frontend stores after merge (MUST FIX)

**Problem confirmed.** `useQualityReportStore.mergeMembers` (useQualityReportStore.ts:83-95) only refreshes the report + member list. The member-delete path (useMemberStore.ts:134, and many sites) additionally calls `invalidateDerivedViews()` and, for merge, the re-pointed content (events, stories, gallery, tasks, documents) is never refreshed on the acting client. The backend merge route only publishes `content_changed` for `domain: "member"` (members.py:457), so SSE won't refresh other domains either.

**Fix (frontend — useQualityReportStore.ts `mergeMembers`):** after a successful merge, match the delete path:
- call `invalidateDerivedViews()` (from `@/hooks/invalidateDerivedViews`) — note this clears the quality report store itself, so order it with the existing `refreshReport` (either refresh then invalidate-others, or invalidate then refresh report; mirror how useMemberStore sequences `refreshMembers` + `invalidateDerivedViews`).
- refresh the per-tree domain stores that merge re-points: `useEventStore.refreshEvents`, `useStoryStore.refreshStories`, `useGalleryStore.refreshGalleryImages`, `useTaskStore` refresh (see the `refreshTaskStore` used in realtime.ts:104), `useDocumentStore.refreshDocuments`. Guard each on `isActiveTree(treeId)`.

**Backend complement (recommended, members.py `merge_members`):** the route should publish `content_changed` for every domain the merge actually touches (event, story, gallery, task, document) — not just member — so **other** connected clients also refresh. The realtime handler already maps those domains (realtime.ts:100-107). Item 1 already adds the `event` domain publish; extend to the rest. This is the more correct fix; the frontend-store change covers the acting client which may not receive its own SSE reliably.

**Decision to flag:** doing both (frontend refresh + broadened SSE) is belt-and-suspenders and matches how the codebase already works elsewhere. Prefer both.

**Tests:**
- `frontend/src/components/view/quality-report-view/MergeMembersDialog.test.tsx` (or a new `useQualityReportStore.test.ts` if one is warranted): assert that after `mergeMembers` resolves, `invalidateDerivedViews`/domain refreshers are invoked. These stores are typically mocked; add spies.
- `backend/tests/test_member_merge.py`: if broadening SSE, assert the published events include the touched domains (there may be an existing pattern capturing `publish_tree_event`; `test_merge_route_records_rich_activity_payload` at line 349 is the closest existing route-level test to extend).

### Item 4b — Data loss by default (treat as MUST-FIX severity)

**Problem confirmed.** `buildInitialResolutionState` (mergeUtils.ts:54-66) defaults **every** conflict to `"a"` (keep's value). `compute_conflicts` (merge.py:124-140) reports one-sided conflicts (keep empty, remove has data) as conflicts. Clicking through with defaults silently discards remove's data — a destructive, irreversible merge. `reconcile_bridge_fields` (merge.py:342-349) already defaults one-sided fields to the non-empty side; the dialog should adopt the same logic.

**Fix (frontend — mergeUtils.ts `buildInitialResolutionState`):** the function needs both members' field values to pick a smart default. It currently only receives `pair` — but `DuplicatePair` carries `member_a`/`member_b` (`MemberOut`), so read `getMemberField(pair.member_a, field)` / `member_b`. For each conflict field: default `"a"` when keep's value is non-empty **or** remove's is empty; else `"b"` (mirrors merge.py:349). Keep `"combine"` off by default. Reuse the existing empty check semantics (add a small `isEmpty` helper matching backend `_empty`: null/blank).
- Confirm the field-name casing: `pair.conflicts` are camelCase (member_merge.py:62) and `MemberOut` fields are camelCase in the frontend `MemberDB` shape, so `getMemberField` works directly.

**Item 4b — image_data:** `compute_conflicts` reports `image_data` **only when both sides are set and differ** (merge.py:130-133). So when only remove has a photo and keep has none, it's not a conflict, not surfaced, and lost (default keep-a-empty wins). Two options — **recommend option 1**:
1. Backend: in `compute_conflicts`, also report `image_data` when exactly one side is non-empty (one-sided), consistent with other fields. Then the smart default (4b above) auto-picks the non-empty side, so a lone remove photo transfers. Keeps everything in the existing conflict-resolution machinery. Note: the dialog renders image conflicts via `MergeConflictResolver` — verify it handles a one-sided image gracefully (shows the one photo).
2. Alternatively, `apply_field_choices`/merge could special-case: if keep's `image_data` is empty and remove's is set and there's no explicit choice, carry remove's over. More hidden magic; less consistent. Prefer option 1.

**Tests:**
- `frontend/src/utils/mergeUtils.test.ts`: one-sided conflict (keep empty, remove set) → initial state defaults to `"b"`; both-set → `"a"`; both-empty (shouldn't be a conflict) unaffected.
- `backend/tests/test_member_merge.py` and/or `test_merge_preview.py`: `compute_conflicts` now reports one-sided `image_data`; a merge with keep-no-photo, remove-photo, default choice → keep ends with remove's `image_data`.

---

## Item 5 — Double success toast (WORTH FLAGGING)

**Problem confirmed.** `MergeMembersDialog.handleConfirm` toasts `t("success")` (MergeMembersDialog.tsx:128) then calls `onMerged()`, which in QualityReportView fires `toast.success(t("merge-success"))` (QualityReportView.tsx:218). Two toasts.

**Fix:** keep exactly one. Recommend removing the toast from `QualityReportView`'s `onMerged` (line 218) and keeping it in the dialog (the dialog owns the success/error mapping already, MergeMembersDialog.tsx:128-136), so `onMerged` becomes a no-op callback or is dropped if unused elsewhere. Verify `onMerged` has no other responsibility (it's only the toast here). No i18n changes; the now-unused `quality-report-view.merge-success` key can stay or be removed (removing needs it gone from both en.json + de.json to keep `check-i18n` green — safer to keep it).

**Tests:** `QualityReportView.test.tsx` / `MergeMembersDialog.test.tsx` — assert exactly one success toast after a merge (update whichever test currently asserts on the toast).

---

## Item 6 — Silent preview failure (WORTH FLAGGING)

**Problem confirmed.** Preview fetch errors are swallowed with `setPreview(null)` (MergeMembersDialog.tsx:93-95); the Merge button stays disabled (`!preview`, line 276) with no explanation.

**Fix (MergeMembersDialog.tsx):** add a `previewError` state; set it in the `.catch` (line 93). Render a visible `text-destructive` message when set and not loading (near the `loading-preview` block, lines 229-233). Clear it at the start of each preview effect. New i18n key `merge-members-dialog.preview-error` in **both** en.json and de.json.

**Interaction with item 3:** if you add `would_create_cycle` to the preview (item 3), that's a *successful* preview with a blocking condition — a distinct message/state from a *failed* preview fetch. Keep them separate: `preview-error` (fetch failed) vs a cycle-warning key.

---

# Implementation Plan — PR #812 review fixes

## Key architectural constraint discovered (affects items 1 & 2)

`backend/app/services/member_merge.py` is imported by `backend/app/api/routes/members.py` (line 68). The helpers the review says to reuse — `_sync_vital_event` (members.py:732), `_sync_bridge_person` (members.py:178), `_event_updates_allowed` (members.py:629) — live in the **route module**. The service therefore cannot call them without a circular import. Two options recur below:

- **Option A (recommended, least churn):** do the post-merge fix-ups in the route handler `merge_members` (members.py:389-472), after `merge_members_in_place` returns and before `db.commit()`. The route already orchestrates activity logging + SSE, and has `user`/`tree` in scope.
- **Option B:** extract `_sync_vital_event` + `_event_updates_allowed` (and optionally `_sync_bridge_person`) into a shared service module and import from both. Cleaner separation but a bigger diff and more test surface.

The plan below assumes Option A unless noted. Whichever is chosen, items 1 and 2 both add post-merge sync that can touch a second tree (the bridge counterpart's), which must then get its own `content_changed`/activity — see the interaction notes.

---

## Item 1 — Vital-event mirror breaks after merge (MUST FIX)

**Problem confirmed.** `merge_members_in_place` (member_merge.py:263) calls `_repoint_member_links(EventMemberLink,...)`, transferring *all* of `remove`'s event links onto `keep`, including derived birth/death mirror `Event` rows. Two failure modes:
- (a) keep + remove each have a birth mirror event → keep ends up linked to two birth events. `_sync_vital_event` (members.py:753) does `events[0]` and assumes exactly one; the second lingers as a stale duplicate in keep's timeline.
- (b) field choice "b" changes keep's `date_of_birth`/`date_of_death`/`birthplace`/`cemetery` → the mirror event is never re-synced (the merge path never calls `_sync_vital_event`, unlike `update_member` at members.py:882-893).

**Fix (route, post-merge — members.py `merge_members`):** after `merge_members_in_place` returns, before `record_activity`:
1. Gate on `_event_updates_allowed(db, tree, user)` to match `update_member` and avoid partial failures when Events is disabled/restricted.
2. **Dedup** keep's vital mirror events: for each of `"birth"`/`"death"`, query `Event` rows of that type linked to `keep.id` via `EventMemberLink` (same query shape as `_sync_vital_event`, members.py:741-752), ordered deterministically; if more than one, keep the first and `db.delete` the rest (their `EventMemberLink` rows cascade — confirm cascade or delete the links explicitly).
3. **Resync** the surviving event to keep's post-merge resolved fields: call `_sync_vital_event(db, tree, keep, "birth", keep.date_of_birth, keep.birthplace)` and `..."death", keep.date_of_death, keep.cemetery)`. This aligns the date and backfills location using the existing #659/#769-safe logic.
4. Publish an extra `tree.content_changed` with `domain: "event"` for `tree` (mirroring `update_member` at members.py:929-935) so timelines refresh — but note item 4 will already broaden domain refresh; keep this consistent.

**Interaction with item 2:** if keep is a bridge person, the resynced/deduped vital event lives only in keep's tree; the counterpart's vital fields are handled by item 2's `_sync_bridge_person`, but the counterpart's *own* mirror events are not touched here (update_member has the same limitation — acceptable, note it).

**Decision to flag:** doing dedup only when `_event_updates_allowed` means a restricted-events editor's merge could still leave a duplicate birth event. The duplicate is a real integrity problem independent of the flag. Recommend: run **dedup unconditionally** (integrity cleanup, like the FK cleanup already done in the merge) but gate only the **date/location resync** on `_event_updates_allowed`. Call this out for the reviewer.

**Tests (`backend/tests/test_member_merge.py`):**
- keep + remove each have a birth mirror event → after merge, keep has exactly one birth event with keep's resolved date (extends the pattern of `test_event_link_transferred` / `test_event_link_duplicate_dropped`).
- field choice "b" adopts remove's `date_of_birth`/`birthplace` → keep's single birth mirror event reflects remove's date/location afterwards (builds on `test_field_choice_b_adopts_remove_value` at line 319).
- events-restricted editor path (if you gate resync) → no crash, links still repointed.

---

## Item 2 — Bridge-person drift (MUST FIX)

**Problem confirmed.** `BRIDGE_SYNC_FIELDS` (bridge.py:16-34) overlaps `CONFLICT_FIELDS` (merge.py:109-121) almost entirely. If keep is a bridge person and field choices adopt remove's values, keep's counterpart in the other tree is never synced. `update_member` handles this via `_sync_bridge_person` (members.py:897); the merge path does not.

**Fix (route, post-merge — members.py `merge_members`):**
1. Compute the set of person-fields that actually changed on keep due to the merge. `merge_members_in_place` already captures `keep_before` (member_merge.py:225) and returns it inside `details["merge"]["keep_before"]`. Either read it from `details`, or (cleaner) have `merge_members_in_place` also return an explicit `changed_fields` dict. Recommend adding `changed_fields` to the return tuple to avoid reaching into the activity payload. Build `changed = {f: getattr(keep, f) for f in CONFLICT_FIELDS if getattr(keep, f) != keep_before[f]}`.
2. Call `_sync_bridge_person(db, keep, changed, user)` (members.py:178). It already filters to `BRIDGE_SYNC_FIELDS`, checks the `tree_links` feature + write access, copies media cross-tree, and returns `(status, synced_tree)`.
3. If `synced_tree` is returned, publish `tree.content_changed` (domain member) + `invalidate_stats` for it, exactly like `update_member` (members.py:937-944).

**Interaction — bridge inherited case:** `merge_members_in_place` may have just *inherited* remove's bridge onto keep (member_merge.py:280-285), setting `keep.linked_member_id` to remove's counterpart. Running `_sync_bridge_person(keep, changed, user)` then pushes keep's resolved identity onto that newly-inherited counterpart — desirable. But the route already logs a bridge activity entry for that counterpart tree (members.py:427-449). Ensure the new `_sync_bridge_person` call and the existing counterpart activity/SSE don't double-publish or conflict for the same tree. Flag this: the "changed_fields" sync and the "inherited link" activity may target the **same** counterpart tree — consolidate the SSE/`invalidate_stats` calls so each tree is published once.

**Signature change flagged:** returning `changed_fields` (or the resolved-changes) from `merge_members_in_place` is the cleanest wiring and keeps the route from parsing `details`.

**Tests (`backend/tests/test_member_merge.py`):** extend the existing bridge tests (`test_bridge_link_inherited_onto_keep_and_logged_in_other_tree` line 383, `test_bridge_link_dissolved...` line 432):
- keep is a bridge person; merge adopts remove's `date_of_birth`/`last_name` via field choice "b" → counterpart in the other tree now has the new values (feature enabled, writer access).
- feature off / no access → counterpart unchanged, no crash (mirrors `_sync_bridge_person`'s `skipped_no_access`).

---

## Item 3 — Cycle guard is over-broad (MUST FIX)

**Problem confirmed.** member_merge.py:193-216 simulates the whole tree's relations and calls `find_parent_cycle_members(remaining_members, simulated_relations)` (quality_checks.py:45), which returns cycle members *anywhere* in the graph. Any pre-existing unrelated cycle → every merge in that tree 400s with "This merge would create a relationship cycle". Relation-creation elsewhere has no cycle guard, and the quality report treats cycles as informational, so this is inconsistent and misleading.

**Fix:** scope the check to cycles **reachable from/involving `keep.id` after the merge**. Replace the whole-graph simulation with a targeted DFS:
1. Build a post-merge parent adjacency in memory: iterate `all_relations`, remap `remove.id → keep.id` on both endpoints, drop self-edges, keep only `relation_type == "parent"` edges (child `from_member_id` → parent `to_member_id`), dedup.
2. Run a DFS starting **from `keep.id`** walking the parent chain; if the traversal revisits `keep.id` (a node on the current stack loops back), it's a merge-created/merge-involving cycle → 400. A cycle not reachable from keep is left alone.
3. This removes the need to fetch `remaining_members` and to build `SimpleNamespace` fakes (ties into item 8).

**Preview decision (flagged):** `get_member_merge_preview` (members.py:606) currently does **not** run any cycle check, so users resolve all conflicts then hit a 400 on confirm. Recommend surfacing the scoped check earlier: add a boolean like `would_create_cycle` to `MemberMergePreviewOut` (schema `backend/app/schemas/merge.py`) computed by `compute_member_merge_preview`, and have the frontend dialog disable Merge + show a message when true. This is a schema field addition (no DB migration — response-only). If you prefer to keep scope tight, at minimum keep the confirm-time 400 but this is the better UX. **This interacts with item 6** (error UI) — the cycle-preview message and the preview-failure message are different states.

**Extract a helper:** put the scoped "does merging remove into keep create a parent cycle reachable from keep" logic in a small function (in member_merge.py or quality_checks.py) so both the confirm path and preview path call the same code.

**Tests:**
- `test_member_merge.py`: keep `test_merge_creates_cycle_is_rejected` (line 96) passing under the new logic. **Add** a test: a pre-existing cycle among *unrelated* members does **not** block merging two other members (this is the regression the fix targets).
- If adding `would_create_cycle` to preview: a preview test asserting the flag flips true for a merge that would loop keep's parent chain.
- `backend/tests/test_quality.py`: unaffected (`find_parent_cycle_members` signature unchanged if you add a separate scoped helper rather than modifying it).

---

## Item 4 — Stale frontend stores after merge (MUST FIX)

**Problem confirmed.** `useQualityReportStore.mergeMembers` (useQualityReportStore.ts:83-95) only refreshes the report + member list. The member-delete path (useMemberStore.ts:134, and many sites) additionally calls `invalidateDerivedViews()` and, for merge, the re-pointed content (events, stories, gallery, tasks, documents) is never refreshed on the acting client. The backend merge route only publishes `content_changed` for `domain: "member"` (members.py:457), so SSE won't refresh other domains either.

**Fix (frontend — useQualityReportStore.ts `mergeMembers`):** after a successful merge, match the delete path:
- call `invalidateDerivedViews()` (from `@/hooks/invalidateDerivedViews`) — note this clears the quality report store itself, so order it with the existing `refreshReport` (either refresh then invalidate-others, or invalidate then refresh report; mirror how useMemberStore sequences `refreshMembers` + `invalidateDerivedViews`).
- refresh the per-tree domain stores that merge re-points: `useEventStore.refreshEvents`, `useStoryStore.refreshStories`, `useGalleryStore.refreshGalleryImages`, `useTaskStore` refresh (see the `refreshTaskStore` used in realtime.ts:104), `useDocumentStore.refreshDocuments`. Guard each on `isActiveTree(treeId)`.

**Backend complement (recommended, members.py `merge_members`):** the route should publish `content_changed` for every domain the merge actually touches (event, story, gallery, task, document) — not just member — so **other** connected clients also refresh. The realtime handler already maps those domains (realtime.ts:100-107). Item 1 already adds the `event` domain publish; extend to the rest. This is the more correct fix; the frontend-store change covers the acting client which may not receive its own SSE reliably.

**Decision to flag:** doing both (frontend refresh + broadened SSE) is belt-and-suspenders and matches how the codebase already works elsewhere. Prefer both.

**Tests:**
- `frontend/src/components/view/quality-report-view/MergeMembersDialog.test.tsx` (or a new `useQualityReportStore.test.ts` if one is warranted): assert that after `mergeMembers` resolves, `invalidateDerivedViews`/domain refreshers are invoked. These stores are typically mocked; add spies.
- `backend/tests/test_member_merge.py`: if broadening SSE, assert the published events include the touched domains (there may be an existing pattern capturing `publish_tree_event`; `test_merge_route_records_rich_activity_payload` at line 349 is the closest existing route-level test to extend).

### Item 4b — Data loss by default (treat as MUST-FIX severity)

**Problem confirmed.** `buildInitialResolutionState` (mergeUtils.ts:54-66) defaults **every** conflict to `"a"` (keep's value). `compute_conflicts` (merge.py:124-140) reports one-sided conflicts (keep empty, remove has data) as conflicts. Clicking through with defaults silently discards remove's data — a destructive, irreversible merge. `reconcile_bridge_fields` (merge.py:342-349) already defaults one-sided fields to the non-empty side; the dialog should adopt the same logic.

**Fix (frontend — mergeUtils.ts `buildInitialResolutionState`):** the function needs both members' field values to pick a smart default. It currently only receives `pair` — but `DuplicatePair` carries `member_a`/`member_b` (`MemberOut`), so read `getMemberField(pair.member_a, field)` / `member_b`. For each conflict field: default `"a"` when keep's value is non-empty **or** remove's is empty; else `"b"` (mirrors merge.py:349). Keep `"combine"` off by default. Reuse the existing empty check semantics (add a small `isEmpty` helper matching backend `_empty`: null/blank).
- Confirm the field-name casing: `pair.conflicts` are camelCase (member_merge.py:62) and `MemberOut` fields are camelCase in the frontend `MemberDB` shape, so `getMemberField` works directly.

**Item 4b — image_data:** `compute_conflicts` reports `image_data` **only when both sides are set and differ** (merge.py:130-133). So when only remove has a photo and keep has none, it's not a conflict, not surfaced, and lost (default keep-a-empty wins). Two options — **recommend option 1**:
1. Backend: in `compute_conflicts`, also report `image_data` when exactly one side is non-empty (one-sided), consistent with other fields. Then the smart default (4b above) auto-picks the non-empty side, so a lone remove photo transfers. Keeps everything in the existing conflict-resolution machinery. Note: the dialog renders image conflicts via `MergeConflictResolver` — verify it handles a one-sided image gracefully (shows the one photo).
2. Alternatively, `apply_field_choices`/merge could special-case: if keep's `image_data` is empty and remove's is set and there's no explicit choice, carry remove's over. More hidden magic; less consistent. Prefer option 1.

**Tests:**
- `frontend/src/utils/mergeUtils.test.ts`: one-sided conflict (keep empty, remove set) → initial state defaults to `"b"`; both-set → `"a"`; both-empty (shouldn't be a conflict) unaffected.
- `backend/tests/test_member_merge.py` and/or `test_merge_preview.py`: `compute_conflicts` now reports one-sided `image_data`; a merge with keep-no-photo, remove-photo, default choice → keep ends with remove's `image_data`.

---

## Item 5 — Double success toast (WORTH FLAGGING)

**Problem confirmed.** `MergeMembersDialog.handleConfirm` toasts `t("success")` (MergeMembersDialog.tsx:128) then calls `onMerged()`, which in QualityReportView fires `toast.success(t("merge-success"))` (QualityReportView.tsx:218). Two toasts.

**Fix:** keep exactly one. Recommend removing the toast from `QualityReportView`'s `onMerged` (line 218) and keeping it in the dialog (the dialog owns the success/error mapping already, MergeMembersDialog.tsx:128-136), so `onMerged` becomes a no-op callback or is dropped if unused elsewhere. Verify `onMerged` has no other responsibility (it's only the toast here). No i18n changes; the now-unused `quality-report-view.merge-success` key can stay or be removed (removing needs it gone from both en.json + de.json to keep `check-i18n` green — safer to keep it).

**Tests:** `QualityReportView.test.tsx` / `MergeMembersDialog.test.tsx` — assert exactly one success toast after a merge (update whichever test currently asserts on the toast).

---

## Item 6 — Silent preview failure (WORTH FLAGGING)

**Problem confirmed.** Preview fetch errors are swallowed with `setPreview(null)` (MergeMembersDialog.tsx:93-95); the Merge button stays disabled (`!preview`, line 276) with no explanation.

**Fix (MergeMembersDialog.tsx):** add a `previewError` state; set it in the `.catch` (line 93). Render a visible `text-destructive` message when set and not loading (near the `loading-preview` block, lines 229-233). Clear it at the start of each preview effect. New i18n key `merge-members-dialog.preview-error` in **both** en.json and de.json.

**Interaction with item 3:** if you add `would_create_cycle` to the preview (item 3), that's a *successful* preview with a blocking condition — a distinct message/state from a *failed* preview fetch. Keep them separate: `preview-error` (fetch failed) vs a cycle-warning key.

**Tests:** `MergeMembersDialog.test.tsx` — mock `getMemberMergePreview` to reject; assert the error message renders and Merge stays disabled.

**i18n keys:** `preview-error` (+ optional `cycle-warning` if item 3 preview flag adopted), en + de.

---

## Item 7 — Preview transfer counts overstate reality (WORTH FLAGGING)

**Problem confirmed.** `compute_member_merge_preview` (member_merge.py:52-99) counts **all** of remove's relations/links via raw `func.count()` (lines 72-97). The actual merge drops duplicates (links already on keep) and self-relations (member_merge.py:230-275). So "N will be transferred" overstates what happens.

**Fix (member_merge.py `compute_member_merge_preview`):** compute counts using the same dedup rules as the merge:
- **Relations:** count remove's relations that, after remapping remove→keep, are neither self-relations nor already present on keep (replicate the keys logic from member_merge.py:231-250 without mutating).
- **Content links (events/stories/gallery/documents/tasks):** count remove's links whose `content_id` is **not** already linked to keep (mirror `_repoint_member_links` dedup, member_merge.py:117-129).
- **Diseases:** count remove's diseases whose normalized name isn't already on keep (mirror `_transfer_diseases`, member_merge.py:143-157).

To avoid drift, consider a shared helper that both the preview and the merge use to compute "what would transfer," but a read-only recount in the preview is acceptable and simpler. Keep it query-light (the members' link sets are small).

**Flag — more involved than it looks:** matching *exactly* requires duplicating four dedup rules; the cleanest long-term fix is to factor the "keys already on keep vs remove's candidates" computation into reusable functions called by both preview and merge. Recommend at least extracting the per-table dedup predicate so preview and merge can't diverge again.

**Note (item 1 overlap):** the event count should also account for vital mirror-event dedup (item 1) so the "events" number matches post-fix reality. Coordinate: whatever dedup item 1 introduces for mirror events, the preview's event count should reflect it (or explicitly document that mirror events are excluded from the transfer count).

**Tests (`test_member_merge.py` / `test_merge_preview.py`):** extend `test_preview_reports_camel_case_conflicts_and_transfer_counts` (line 40): set up remove with a duplicate event link + a self-relation + a duplicate disease, assert the preview counts match what the merge actually transfers (cross-check by running the merge and counting).

---

## Item 8 — Style: private imports + SimpleNamespace type-lie (WORTH FLAGGING)

**Problem confirmed.** member_merge.py:39-46 imports `_norm`, `_to_snake_case` (private) from `app.services.merge`. And the cycle guard builds `SimpleNamespace` objects (member_merge.py:203) passed to `find_parent_cycle_members(..., relations: list[Relation])` — a type-hint lie.

**Fix:**
- Promote `_norm` → `norm` and `_to_snake_case` → `to_snake_case` in merge.py (merge.py:62, 74), update both internal uses in merge.py and the imports/uses in member_merge.py. Keep them in merge.py (or move to a small `normalization`/text utils module if preferred). Grep for any other importers of the underscore names before renaming.
- **SimpleNamespace cleanup falls out of item 3:** the scoped DFS (item 3) builds a plain in-memory parent adjacency dict and no longer needs `find_parent_cycle_members` with fake `Relation`s at all. So the `SimpleNamespace(...)` (member_merge.py:196-206) and the `remaining_members` fetch (207-211) disappear. **Do item 3 and item 8's SimpleNamespace part together** — the type-lie is removed as a natural consequence, not patched separately. If for some reason item 3 keeps calling `find_parent_cycle_members`, then instead relax its type hints to a `Protocol`/structural type rather than `list[Relation]`.

**Tests:** pure refactor — existing `test_member_merge.py` + `test_merge.py` + `test_merge_preview.py` must stay green (they exercise the renamed helpers indirectly). Grep tests for direct `_norm`/`_to_snake_case` references and update.

---

## Cross-cutting: i18n, CHANGELOG, migrations, CI

- **i18n:** only `en.json` and `de.json` exist (`frontend/src/i18n/locales/`) — confirmed. New keys: item 6 `merge-members-dialog.preview-error` (+ optional `cycle-warning`). Any removed key (item 5) must be removed from **both** locales or left in both. Run `npm run check-i18n`.
- **CHANGELOG.md:** there is already an Unreleased `Added` bullet for #729 (lines 14-25). These are bug fixes to an **unreleased** feature, so do **not** add new `Fixed` bullets — instead **amend** the existing #729 `Added` bullet if any user-visible behavior described there is now wrong (e.g. it already says the merge "refuses to run if it would create a relationship cycle" — after item 3 that becomes "…create a cycle involving the kept record," worth tightening). No separate `Fixed` section needed since the feature never shipped. Flag for the human: confirm this PR is still pre-release.
- **Migrations:** none of the 9 items need a schema change. Item 3's optional `would_create_cycle` and item 4b's `image_data` conflict are response-shape/logic changes, not DB columns. **Confirmed: no Alembic migration required.**
- **CI parity:** frontend `npm run build` + `npx vitest run` + `npm run check-i18n`; backend `uv run ruff check` + `uv run pytest`.

## Item interactions to keep in front of mind
- **3 ↔ 8:** the DFS rework deletes the SimpleNamespace type-lie; do them as one change.
- **3 ↔ 6:** the optional preview cycle flag creates a new "blocked but preview succeeded" state distinct from item 6's "preview failed" state — separate messages.
- **1 ↔ 7:** mirror-event dedup changes the true event transfer count; keep the preview's event count consistent.
- **1 ↔ 2 ↔ 4:** all three add post-merge side effects (vital resync, bridge sync, broadened SSE) that can touch a second tree; consolidate the per-tree `publish_tree_event`/`invalidate_stats` calls in the route so each affected tree is published exactly once.

"""In-place, same-tree member merge (#729).

Unlike ``app.services.merge`` (which clones two whole *trees* into a brand
new third tree), this combines two *members of the same tree*: one survives
(``keep``), the other is removed (``remove``) after everything it owns —
relations, content links, diseases, and an optional tree-in-tree bridge — has
been re-pointed onto ``keep``. Field-conflict detection/resolution is reused
from ``app.services.merge`` rather than forked.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from types import SimpleNamespace
from typing import Literal

from fastapi import HTTPException
from pydantic.alias_generators import to_camel
from sqlalchemy import func, or_, select
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from app.models import (
    DocumentMemberLink,
    EventMemberLink,
    GalleryMemberLink,
    Member,
    MemberDisease,
    MemberTaskLink,
    Relation,
    StoryMemberLink,
    Tree,
)
from app.schemas.family import MemberOut
from app.schemas.merge import (
    DuplicatePair,
    MemberMergePreviewOut,
    MemberMergeTransferCounts,
)
from app.services.activity import SNAPSHOT_VERSION, member_delete_snapshot
from app.services.merge import (
    CONFLICT_FIELDS,
    _norm,
    _to_snake_case,
    apply_field_choices,
    compute_conflicts,
    member_key,
)
from app.services.quality_checks import find_parent_cycle_members

BridgeOutcome = Literal["inherited", "dissolved"]


def compute_member_merge_preview(
    db: Session, tree: Tree, keep: Member, remove: Member
) -> MemberMergePreviewOut:
    """Field conflicts plus counts of what a merge would transfer onto ``keep``.

    Conflicts are reported in camelCase (unlike the tree-merge preview, whose
    ``conflicts`` are the raw snake_case attribute names) so the response
    lines up with the frontend's ``RESOLVABLE_FIELDS``/``MergeConflictResolver``
    without a translation layer on the client.
    """
    conflicts = [to_camel(field) for field in compute_conflicts(keep, remove)]
    match = "exact" if member_key(keep) == member_key(remove) else "possible"
    pair = DuplicatePair(
        member_a=MemberOut.model_validate(keep),
        member_b=MemberOut.model_validate(remove),
        match=match,
        conflicts=conflicts,
        default_action="merge",
    )

    def _count(model: type, column) -> int:
        return db.scalar(select(func.count()).where(column == remove.id)) or 0

    relations = (
        db.scalar(
            select(func.count())
            .select_from(Relation)
            .where(
                Relation.tree_id == tree.id,
                or_(
                    Relation.from_member_id == remove.id,
                    Relation.to_member_id == remove.id,
                ),
            )
        )
        or 0
    )

    transfer = MemberMergeTransferCounts(
        relations=relations,
        events=_count(EventMemberLink, EventMemberLink.member_id),
        stories=_count(StoryMemberLink, StoryMemberLink.member_id),
        gallery=_count(GalleryMemberLink, GalleryMemberLink.member_id),
        documents=_count(DocumentMemberLink, DocumentMemberLink.member_id),
        tasks=_count(MemberTaskLink, MemberTaskLink.member_id),
        diseases=_count(MemberDisease, MemberDisease.member_id),
    )
    return MemberMergePreviewOut(pair=pair, transfer=transfer)


def _repoint_member_links(
    db: Session,
    model: type,
    id_field: str,
    keep_id: str,
    remove_id: str,
    extra_fields: tuple[str, ...] = (),
) -> None:
    """Union a member-link table onto ``keep_id``, dropping duplicates.

    Every content link table (events, stories, gallery, documents, tasks) has
    the same composite-PK shape: ``(<content>_id, member_id)``. A link already
    on ``keep_id`` wins; ``remove_id``'s copy is simply dropped rather than
    causing a primary-key clash.
    """
    keep_ids = {
        getattr(row, id_field)
        for row in db.scalars(select(model).where(model.member_id == keep_id))
    }
    to_add: list[dict] = []
    for row in db.scalars(select(model).where(model.member_id == remove_id)):
        content_id = getattr(row, id_field)
        extras = {field: getattr(row, field) for field in extra_fields}
        db.delete(row)
        if content_id in keep_ids:
            continue
        keep_ids.add(content_id)
        to_add.append({id_field: content_id, "member_id": keep_id, **extras})
    db.flush()
    for kwargs in to_add:
        db.add(model(**kwargs))


def _transfer_diseases(db: Session, keep_id: str, remove_id: str) -> None:
    """Move ``remove``'s disease records onto ``keep``, deduping by name.

    Mirrors the tree-merge dedup policy (``app.services.merge``, diseases
    section): two rows naming the same condition on the same person are
    noise once the two records describe one person, so the duplicate is
    dropped rather than kept alongside.
    """
    keep_names = {
        _norm(d.name)
        for d in db.scalars(
            select(MemberDisease).where(MemberDisease.member_id == keep_id)
        )
    }
    for disease in db.scalars(
        select(MemberDisease).where(MemberDisease.member_id == remove_id)
    ):
        name_key = _norm(disease.name)
        if name_key in keep_names:
            db.delete(disease)
            continue
        keep_names.add(name_key)
        disease.member_id = keep_id
    # Flush now (mirroring _repoint_member_links) so these deletes/updates
    # reach the DB before the caller deletes `remove` — otherwise the FK
    # cascade on that delete can race the still-pending disease writes.
    db.flush()


def merge_members_in_place(
    db: Session,
    tree: Tree,
    keep: Member,
    remove: Member,
    fields: dict[str, str],
) -> tuple[Member, dict, Member | None, BridgeOutcome | None]:
    """Merge ``remove`` into ``keep`` within ``tree``; caller commits.

    Returns ``(keep, activity_details, counterpart, bridge_outcome)`` —
    ``counterpart`` is the bridge-person row in another tree, set only when
    ``remove`` was linked to one; ``bridge_outcome`` says what happened to it
    (``"inherited"`` onto ``keep``, or ``"dissolved"`` because ``keep`` already
    had its own link) so the route can log it and notify that other tree.
    """
    if keep.id == remove.id:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=400, detail="Cannot merge a member with itself"
        )

    normalized_fields = {
        snake: choice
        for snake, choice in (
            (_to_snake_case(field), choice) for field, choice in fields.items()
        )
        if snake in CONFLICT_FIELDS
    }

    # --- Cycle guard: simulate folding remove's edges onto keep first -------
    all_relations = list(
        db.scalars(select(Relation).where(Relation.tree_id == tree.id))
    )
    simulated_relations = []
    for r in all_relations:
        f = keep.id if r.from_member_id == remove.id else r.from_member_id
        t = keep.id if r.to_member_id == remove.id else r.to_member_id
        if f == t:
            continue
        simulated_relations.append(
            SimpleNamespace(
                from_member_id=f, to_member_id=t, relation_type=r.relation_type
            )
        )
    remaining_members = [
        m
        for m in db.scalars(select(Member).where(Member.tree_id == tree.id))
        if m.id != remove.id
    ]
    if find_parent_cycle_members(remaining_members, simulated_relations):
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=400,
            detail="This merge would create a relationship cycle",
        )

    # --- Pre-image for the activity log, captured before any mutation -------
    counterpart: Member | None = (
        db.get(Member, remove.linked_member_id)
        if remove.linked_member_id is not None
        else None
    )
    removed_snapshot = member_delete_snapshot(db, remove, counterpart)["snapshot"]
    keep_before = {field: getattr(keep, field) for field in CONFLICT_FIELDS}

    # --- Field resolution onto keep (keep=clone=ma, remove=mb) --------------
    apply_field_choices(keep, keep, remove, normalized_fields)

    # --- Relations: union onto keep, dedupe, drop self-relations -----------
    keep_keys: set[tuple[str, str, str]] = set()
    remove_relations: list[Relation] = []
    for r in all_relations:
        if remove.id in (r.from_member_id, r.to_member_id):
            remove_relations.append(r)
        else:
            keep_keys.add((r.from_member_id, r.to_member_id, r.relation_type))

    new_relations: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = []
    for r in remove_relations:
        f = keep.id if r.from_member_id == remove.id else r.from_member_id
        t = keep.id if r.to_member_id == remove.id else r.to_member_id
        db.delete(r)
        if f == t:
            continue  # self-relation once both ends fold onto keep
        key = (f, t, r.relation_type)
        if key in keep_keys:
            continue  # keep already has this relation
        keep_keys.add(key)
        new_relations.append(key)
    db.flush()
    for f, t, relation_type in new_relations:
        db.add(
            Relation(
                tree_id=tree.id,
                from_member_id=f,
                to_member_id=t,
                relation_type=relation_type,
            )
        )

    # --- Content links: union onto keep, dedupe ------------------------------
    _repoint_member_links(db, EventMemberLink, "event_id", keep.id, remove.id)
    _repoint_member_links(db, StoryMemberLink, "story_id", keep.id, remove.id)
    _repoint_member_links(
        db,
        GalleryMemberLink,
        "gallery_image_id",
        keep.id,
        remove.id,
        extra_fields=("x", "y", "w", "h"),
    )
    _repoint_member_links(db, DocumentMemberLink, "document_id", keep.id, remove.id)
    _repoint_member_links(db, MemberTaskLink, "task_id", keep.id, remove.id)
    _transfer_diseases(db, keep.id, remove.id)

    # --- Tree-in-tree bridge: carry the link onto keep, else dissolve it ----
    bridge_outcome: BridgeOutcome | None = None
    if counterpart is not None:
        if keep.linked_member_id is None:
            keep.linked_tree_id = remove.linked_tree_id
            keep.linked_member_id = remove.linked_member_id
            counterpart.linked_tree_id = keep.tree_id
            counterpart.linked_member_id = keep.id
            bridge_outcome = "inherited"
        else:
            counterpart.linked_tree_id = None
            counterpart.linked_member_id = None
            bridge_outcome = "dissolved"

    details = {
        "merge": {
            "version": SNAPSHOT_VERSION,
            "keep_id": keep.id,
            "removed": removed_snapshot,
            "keep_before": keep_before,
            "field_choices": normalized_fields,
        }
    }

    db.delete(remove)
    return keep, details, counterpart, bridge_outcome

281	def apply_field_choices(
282	    clone: Member,
283	    ma: Member,
284	    mb: Member,
285	    fields: dict[str, str],
286	) -> None:
287	    """Apply per-field resolution choices to a merged clone.
288	
289	    ``clone`` was already built from ``ma`` (source A); we apply overrides here.
290	    ``fields`` maps field_name → "a" | "b" | "combine".
291	    """
292	    text_fields = {"additional_data", "places_lived"}
293	    for field, choice in fields.items():
294	        if field not in CONFLICT_FIELDS:
295	            continue
296	        va = getattr(ma, field, None)
297	        vb = getattr(mb, field, None)
298	        if choice == "a":
299	            setattr(clone, field, va)
300	        elif choice == "b":
301	            setattr(clone, field, vb)
302	        elif choice == "combine" and field in text_fields:
303	            separator = "\n\n" if field == "additional_data" else ", "
304	            parts = [p for p in [va, vb] if not _empty(p)]
305	            # Deduplicate while preserving order
306	            seen: list[str] = []
307	            for p in parts:
308	                if p not in seen:
309	                    seen.append(p)
310	            setattr(clone, field, separator.join(seen) if seen else None)

313	def reconcile_bridge_fields(
314	    member: Member,
315	    counterpart: Member,
316	    choices: dict[str, str] | None = None,
317	) -> None:
318	    """Reconcile the conflicting fields of a freshly-wired bridge pair.
319	
320	    Used by the link-existing-tree flow (mode="existing") right after
321	    ``_wire_bridge``: the two rows represent the same human, so once linked
322	    their conflicting fields (dates, places, images, notes, ...) should agree
323	    on both sides, not just drift until a later edit or bridge-sync.
324	
325	    For each field in ``CONFLICT_FIELDS`` an explicit choice ("a" | "b" |
326	    "combine", a = ``member``, b = ``counterpart``) from ``choices`` is
327	    applied when given; otherwise the fields are unioned (whichever side is
328	    non-empty wins, preferring ``member`` when both are set) via the same
329	    a/b/combine semantics as ``apply_field_choices``. ``image_data`` is copied
330	    into the destination tree's media store, mirroring
331	    ``bridge.copy_bridge_fields``.
332	
333	    ``choices`` keys may be camelCase (as sent by the frontend, matching its
334	    ``RESOLVABLE_FIELDS``) or snake_case; both are normalised to the
335	    ``Member`` attribute name.
336	    """
337	    choices = choices or {}
338	    normalised_choices = {_to_snake_case(k): v for k, v in choices.items()}
339	    resolved: dict[str, str] = {
340	        k: v for k, v in normalised_choices.items() if k in CONFLICT_FIELDS
341	    }
342	    for field in CONFLICT_FIELDS:
343	        if field in resolved:
344	            continue
345	        va = getattr(member, field, None)
346	        vb = getattr(counterpart, field, None)
347	        # Union default: prefer whichever side is non-empty; when both are
348	        # set (a genuine conflict with no explicit choice) keep A's value.
349	        resolved[field] = "a" if not _empty(va) or _empty(vb) else "b"
350	
351	    # Snapshot pre-reconciliation values so both a→b and b→a copies read the
352	    # same source data even though `member` is mutated first below.
353	    orig_member = {f: getattr(member, f, None) for f in CONFLICT_FIELDS}
354	    orig_counterpart = {f: getattr(counterpart, f, None) for f in CONFLICT_FIELDS}
355	
356	    for field, choice in resolved.items():
357	        if choice == "a":
358	            value = orig_member[field]
359	        elif choice == "b":
360	            value = orig_counterpart[field]
361	        else:  # combine
362	            if field in {"additional_data", "places_lived"}:
363	                separator = "\n\n" if field == "additional_data" else ", "
364	                parts = [
365	                    p for p in [orig_member[field], orig_counterpart[field]]
366	                    if not _empty(p)
367	                ]
368	                seen: list[str] = []
369	                for p in parts:
370	                    if p not in seen:
371	                        seen.append(p)
372	                value = separator.join(seen) if seen else None
373	            else:
374	                # Combine doesn't apply to non-text fields; fall back to A.
375	                value = orig_member[field]
376	
377	        if field == "image_data":
378	            member.image_data = (
379	                value if value == orig_member["image_data"]
380	                else copy_media_to_tree(value, member.tree_id)
381	            )
382	            counterpart.image_data = (
383	                value if value == orig_counterpart["image_data"]
384	                else copy_media_to_tree(value, counterpart.tree_id)
385	            )
386	        else:
387	            setattr(member, field, value)
388	            setattr(counterpart, field, value)

442	    dedup: dict[tuple, Member] = {}
443	    # name-key index for possible-candidate detection
444	    name_index: dict[tuple, tuple[Member, str]] = {}  # name_key → (clone, original_a_id)
445	
446	    # Collect all members from source A first
447	    members_a = list(db.scalars(select(Member).where(Member.tree_id == tree_a.id)))
448	    members_b = (
449	        list(db.scalars(select(Member).where(Member.tree_id == tree_b.id)))
450	        if tree_b
451	        else []
452	    )
453	
454	    # ---- Pass 1: clone all source-A members ----
455	    for ma in members_a:
456	        new_id = str(uuid4())
457	        member_map[ma.id] = new_id
458	        clone = _clone_member(ma, new_tree.id, new_id)
459	        db.add(clone)
460	        dedup[member_key(ma)] = clone
461	        name_index[member_name_key(ma)] = (clone, ma.id)
462	
463	    # ---- Pass 2: process source-B members ----
464	    for mb in members_b:
465	        exact_key = member_key(mb)
466	        name_key = member_name_key(mb)
467	
468	        # --- Check resolution for this pair (if any) ---
469	        # We need to find the matching source-A member to look up the resolution.
470	        matched_a_clone: Member | None = dedup.get(exact_key)
471	        matched_a_id: str | None = None
472	        match_type: str | None = None
473	
474	        if matched_a_clone is not None:
475	            # Exact match found
476	            # Find the original A member id from the member_map (reverse lookup)
477	            for orig_id, new_id in member_map.items():
478	                if new_id == matched_a_clone.id:
479	                    matched_a_id = orig_id
480	                    break
481	            match_type = "exact"
482	        elif name_key in name_index:
483	            # Possible candidate (name+gender match, dates differ)
484	            matched_a_clone, matched_a_id = name_index[name_key]
485	            match_type = "possible"
486	
487	        if matched_a_id is not None and matched_a_clone is not None:
488	            res_key = frozenset({matched_a_id, mb.id})
489	            resolution = res_index.get(res_key)
490	
491	            if match_type == "exact":
492	                # Default behaviour: merge (unless keep_both resolution)
493	                action = resolution.action if resolution else "merge"
494	            else:
495	                # Possible candidate: default keep_both (unless merge resolution)
496	                action = resolution.action if resolution else "keep_both"
497	
498	            if action == "keep_both":
499	                # Clone B as a separate member
500	                new_id = str(uuid4())
501	                member_map[mb.id] = new_id
502	                clone_b = _clone_member(mb, new_tree.id, new_id)
503	                db.add(clone_b)
504	            else:
505	                # Merge: B maps to A's clone; apply field choices if given
506	                member_map[mb.id] = matched_a_clone.id
507	                if resolution and resolution.fields:
508	                    # Find the original A member for field comparison
509	                    orig_ma = next(
510	                        (m for m in members_a if m.id == matched_a_id), None
511	                    )
512	                    if orig_ma is not None:
513	                        apply_field_choices(
514	                            matched_a_clone, orig_ma, mb, resolution.fields
515	                        )
516	                else:
517	                    # Legacy behaviour: combine additional_data
518	                    if (
519	                        mb.additional_data
520	                        and mb.additional_data != matched_a_clone.additional_data
521	                    ):
522	                        matched_a_clone.additional_data = (
523	                            f"{matched_a_clone.additional_data}\n\n{mb.additional_data}"
524	                            if matched_a_clone.additional_data
525	                            else mb.additional_data
526	                        )
527	        else:
528	            # No match: always clone as new
529	            new_id = str(uuid4())
530	            member_map[mb.id] = new_id
531	            clone = _clone_member(mb, new_tree.id, new_id)
532	            db.add(clone)
533	
534	    # Members must exist before relations/diseases/links reference them.
535	    db.flush()
536	    _progress(50)
537	
538	    # --- Relations ---------------------------------------------------------
539	    seen_relations: set[tuple] = set()
540	    for t in sources:
541	        for r in db.scalars(select(Relation).where(Relation.tree_id == t.id)):

543	            to = member_map.get(r.to_member_id)

555	                    )

603	                }

609	            new_task_id = str(uuid4())
610	            seen_tasks[key] = new_task_id

693	                        ),
694	                        created_at=face.created_at,
695	                    )
696	                )

698	    _progress(70)
699	
700	    # --- Events + links ----------------------------------------------------
701	    event_map: dict[str, str] = {}
702	    for t in sources:
703	        for e in db.scalars(select(Event).where(Event.tree_id == t.id)):

719	    for t in sources:

721	            select(EventMemberLink)
722	            .join(Event, Event.id == EventMemberLink.event_id)
723	            .where(Event.tree_id == t.id)
724	        )

731	
732	    _progress(80)
733	
734	    # --- Stories + links ---------------------------------------------------
735	    story_map: dict[str, str] = {}

752	    for t in sources:
